key_insight: Use random features only in interface-cut cells and standard finite elements elsewhere, coupled through a localized hybrid scheme that enforces interface jumps and flux continuity on unfitted meshes.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical way to solve challenging elliptic interface problems with high coefficient contrast and complex geometry while avoiding fully mesh-conforming remeshing.
method: RFM is restricted to the narrow cut-cell band on both sides of the physical interface.
Standard Q_p finite elements are kept on uncut background cells.
A Schur reduction removes interior FEM unknowns, leaving a reduced least-squares problem for coupling nodes and random-feature coefficients.
evidence_signal: The method is numerically tested on 2D and 3D interface problems with high contrasts, nonsmooth and multiple interfaces, irregular outer boundaries, and a thermal-homogenization example.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurate interface localization and stable coupling across the artificial interface, which may complicate implementation for highly intricate geometries.
paper_title: A Localized Hybrid Finite Element--Random Feature Method for Elliptic Interface Problems on Unfitted Meshes
